thread:
jess-support: customer reported that free-trial credits didn't decrement for a bunch of chat streaming sessions yesterday. they saw the usage graph tick once, then multiple streams show 0 consumption even though tokens were generated on the client side. attaching customer repro steps and logs below.

liam-billing: thanks for the flag — can you paste the customer id + sample request id so I can query ledger?

jess-support: customer id cust_43X, request ids: r_20260301_1, r_20260301_2, r_20260301_3. they say they opened 3 parallel streaming connections with the same session_id (session_9a) and sent ~450 tokens each. only r_20260301_1 shows a debit in the billing ledger.

maya-sre: this smells like the session-based dedupe path. runtime dedupes prefix tokens per session to avoid double-charging if the client reconnects quickly. but it shouldn't dedupe across concurrent sockets. do we have logs for the stream attach/detach?

jess-support: pasted trimmed logs from their client below (sanitized):

```
// client log
connect session=session_9a stream=ws-1
sent: {role: user, content: "long prompt A..."} // ~450 tokens
server: 200 streaming start id=r_20260301_1
connect session=session_9a stream=ws-2
sent: {role: user, content: "long prompt B..."} // ~430 tokens
server: 200 streaming start id=r_20260301_2
connect session=session_9a stream=ws-3
sent: {role: user, content: "long prompt C..."} // ~470 tokens
server: 200 streaming start id=r_20260301_3
// client experienced slow first bytes on ws-2, retried by opening ws-4 with same session
connect session=session_9a stream=ws-4
sent: {role: user, content: "long prompt B..."} // retry
server: 200 streaming start id=r_20260301_4
// user cancelled ws-2 and ws-4 quickly, kept ws-1 and ws-3 open until completion
```

maya-sre: interesting. their pattern includes concurrent streams + retries + shared session_id. I can see how a naive session-level prefix cache could consider tokens already accounted for and skip billing on subsequent streams.

ali-runtime: jumping in. we have a `session_prefix_cache` that stores the last-seen token hash per session_id for 5m and a flag `seen_for_billing`. when a stream starts we check `if prefix_hash in cache and cache[hash].billed == true: mark_stream_as_nonbillable()` — this was meant for quick reconnects on the same socket. but I see two issues: 1) we treat any concurrent attach as equivalent to a reconnect, 2) the billing write is performed asynchronously and can race, so if stream A finishes and sets billed=true after stream B already started we flip B to non-billable.

liam-billing: can you point me to the ledger rows for the request ids? I queried payments.usage where request_id in (...) and got only r_20260301_1 and r_20260301_3 present. r_20260301_2 and r_20260301_4 missing. sample query: `select request_id, tokens, debit, created_at from payments.usage where customer_id='cust_43X' and created_at >= '2026-03-01';` returned two rows.

jess-support: the customer is asking for a manual credit for the missing debits — they used up trial allocation but UI still shows ~2/3 credits left because debits weren't applied. they're upset.

maya-sre: ok root cause hypothesis: session_prefix_cache treats any concurrent attach with identical prefix_hash as duplicate and suppresses billing. this combined with async billing write/race means some parallel streams never wrote usage rows. we'll need a quick mitigation.

ali-runtime: quick mitigation suggestion: change check to only dedupe within the same socket_id OR require an explicit `reconnect=true` header. simpler: require stream start to include a `connection_id` that must match reconnection attempts; if missing, treat as distinct and bill. immediate hotfix: stop honoring session_prefix_cache.billed for 30s after creation (so concurrent attaches in that window still bill).

liam-billing: for the customer fix I can create manual debits for the missing two request ids and adjust their free-trial ledger. confirm tokens to bill: r_20260301_2 => 430 tokens, r_20260301_4 => 430 tokens. total 860 tokens. what's the free-trial unit conversion?

jess-support: their account shows free_trial_credits_units = 10000 (in token units). please apply 860 tokens equivalent from that bucket and add a note: "manual adjustment for session dedupe bug - March 1st".

liam-billing: done — created internal transactions: adj_tx_8801 and adj_tx_8802, debited 860 tokens from free_trial_credits_units. pinged customer that we've applied the manual correction and apologised.

ali-runtime: patch plan — I'll submit a PR that 1) narrows dedupe to connection_id, 2) makes the billing write synchronous (fast-path) or at least strongly ordered, and 3) logs explicit reason when stream deemed non-billable. PR will also add an integration test that spins up N concurrent streams with same session_id and asserts all produce usage rows unless connection_id marks reconnect.

maya-sre: rolling a hotfix that sets cache.billed ttl=30s to avoid races and enabling extra logging now. if tests look good we can ship the full fix in next minor release.

sre-bot: deploy job started for hotfix branch `hotfix/dedupe-session-ttl` by maya-sre — build 20260301.1

ali-runtime: thanks all. jess, can you close the support ticket after customer confirmation? also file an incident with the postmortem template capturing root cause + corrective actions (manual credits, hotfix, runtime PR, test).

jess-support: will do. customer acknowledged the manual credit and is fine for now, they asked only for a note in the account. closing ticket and filing incident.

maya-sre: tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime @billing @support — we should audit other code paths that use session-level dedupe for streaming and embeddings.

liam-billing: noted. thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
